public_payload.normalized_proposition: In 2025 OpenAI and Anthropic combined had under $20 billion in revenue (89% of AI startup revenue) while spending at least $30 billion on cloud compute.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic combined to less than $20 billion in annual revenue in 2025 representing 89% of all AI startup revenues, and spent at least $30 billion on compute on Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services.

from_speaker: combined to less than $20 billion in annual revenue in 2025
spent at least $30 billion on compute
Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services
our_interpretation: Read the sentence as three claims about calendar 2025: combined realized revenue, its share of all AI-startup revenue, and combined realized compute spending with the three named providers.
Annual revenue means recognized revenue for the year, not an annualized monthly run rate.
Read 89% as a whole-percentage-point rounded share, requiring a defined and adequately covered AI-startup population.
Do not count multi-year commitments, financing, total research expense, or total operating expense as realized cloud-compute spending.

The percentage links to press analysis and therefore has an estimate basis. The revenue and compute clauses identify no accounting basis; the compound financial scope is consequently unknown rather than silently assigning one basis to all three measures.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence establishes combined realized 2025 revenue below $20 billion, a share rounding to 89% of a defined all-AI-startup revenue total, and at least $30 billion actually spent on compute with the named providers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable same-period evidence establishes combined revenue at least $20 billion, a materially different sector share, or combined spending below $30 billion. A different-year run-rate statistic alone does not establish the actual 2025 share.
